primary_category.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: I did notice the item was irregular, not on a pallet, heavier than usual... stopping to hand-verify felt like it would eat time I didn't have, so I went with what the system gave me.
evidence.explanation: The worker evaluates cargo characteristics against a possible manual verification source and decides whether to retrieve/confirm information before acting.

evidence.quote: I looked at the total weight, saw it was in line with the LMCs we'd been getting all week on this route... and cleared it on that basis
evidence.explanation: The worker retrieves comparative historical data and evaluates whether it is sufficient to clear a load change.

evidence.quote: I pulled the dispatch log for a quick check, given the tail-heavy call from the ramp. Saw the previous two flights on this same rotation... had both needed aft trim corrections.
evidence.explanation: The worker actively retrieves records (dispatch log) and evaluates them against current conditions to inform a decision.

evidence.quote: I shifted some cargo forward beyond what my own index actually required.
evidence.explanation: Reference to a calculated 'index' and quantitative redistribution shows numerical weight-and-balance computation as a core task element.

evidence.quote: A few extra minutes at the trim computer... I didn't think it was worth the time against the schedule.
evidence.explanation: Running an index-shift calculation is an explicit numerical task the worker considered and weighed.

evidence.quote: Two in a row felt like it meant something about how the rotation was running that day
evidence.explanation: The worker forms a generalized explanatory model (a 'rotation-level' condition) from discrete prior events, an abstraction/diagnostic operation beyond simple information retrieval.

evidence.quote: so I shifted some cargo forward beyond what my own index actually required
evidence.explanation: The worker devises and applies a compensatory loading adjustment as a non-routine response to a perceived risk, combining information into a corrective plan under compressed time.

evidence.quote: I issued the ALI to the ramp basically as generated so they could start loading immediately.
evidence.explanation: The worker directs and sequences another team's (ramp crew) activity by issuing instructions, coordinating dependent work under a time constraint.

not_observed_or_insufficient: A1.1 Strength - no evidence the participant performs physical handling; loading is done by 'the ramp', a separate team.
A1.2 Dexterity - no evidence of manual fine-motor operation by the participant.
A1.3 Navigation - no evidence of the participant physically moving through a spatial environment.
A2.1 Uncodified visual/auditory processing - the tail-heavy observation is reported via a ramp phone call, not the participant's own perceptual detection.
A3.1 Serving and attending - no direct service interaction with a customer/passenger described.
A3.3 Selling and influencing - not described.
ambiguities: The trim-sheet redistribution (decision point 3) sits between A2.5 (diagnostic generalization from prior flights) and A2.6 (devising a corrective loading plan); both are retained as secondary since the episode involves both forming an explanation and generating a response.

evidence.quote: I signed and released with the figures as they stood. I weighed the delay risk against a one-bag discrepancy
evidence.explanation: The participant independently makes final sign-off decisions on load, trim, and discrepancy handling without describing supervisor approval in the moment.

evidence.quote: check weight and balance against structural limits, and finalize the NOTOC for the captain
evidence.explanation: Work is bounded by structural limits and a downstream approval chain (the NOTOC goes to the captain), indicating procedural and role-based oversight, though not moment-to-moment supervision.

evidence.quote: About fifteen minutes later, the ramp called and said the aircraft was sitting slightly tail-heavy
evidence.explanation: The participant depends on real-time information exchange with the ramp crew to detect and respond to load conditions, indicating meaningful but not constant collaboration.

evidence.quote: Normally I build the load sheet, issue the loading instruction to the ramp, check weight and balance against structural limits, and finalize the NOTOC
evidence.explanation: The participant describes a standard recurring sequence of tasks performed on each turnaround.

evidence.quote: There is [a manual chart], for exactly that situation. I know where it is.
evidence.explanation: Existence of a specific manual chart for irregular cargo indicates prescribed procedures governing exceptions, alongside a standard ALI/NOTOC workflow.

evidence.quote: Nothing about the flight itself was unusual—same route, same aircraft type—it was just less time to work with.
evidence.explanation: Core flight parameters were predictable, but multiple unplanned inputs (late aircraft, irregular cargo, LMC, discrepancy) reduced certainty within the episode.

evidence.quote: an LMC came in—about 380 kilos of mail plus six late bags that missed the original manifest... the ramp tally was one bag short of the NOTOC and manifest
evidence.explanation: Multiple unplanned disruptions (late-load change, tail-heavy report, tally mismatch) required the participant to adapt procedures in real time under compressed time.

tools.role_in_task: Automated load-instruction and trim/index calculation for weight-and-balance management

evidence.quote: Our load-control software generates an automatic load instruction, and it put that machinery item into hold 3.
evidence.explanation: A purpose-built load-control system generating loading instructions is a specialised professional software tool distinct from general office ICT.

evidence.quote: A few extra minutes at the trim computer.
evidence.explanation: A dedicated 'trim computer' for index/moment calculations is specialised aviation weight-and-balance technology.

tools.role_in_task: Retrieval of historical flight/dispatch records for comparison

evidence.quote: I pulled the dispatch log for a quick check
evidence.explanation: Accessing a dispatch log resembles routine digital record retrieval, though the text does not specify whether this is part of the same specialised system or a separate basic database.

task_anchors.task_description: Reviewing an automated load instruction for an atypical cargo item and deciding whether to issue it as generated or perform independent verification.
Evaluating a late load change for weight and placement, deciding whether full index recalculation is needed.
Interpreting rotation trim history and adjusting cargo placement beyond the calculated index requirement.
Weighing a minor manifest/tally discrepancy against slot-timing pressure before signing and releasing the load documentation.

evidence: I issued the ALI to the ramp basically as generated so they could start loading immediately.
I looked at the total weight, saw it was in line with the LMCs we'd been getting all week on this route... and cleared it on that basis
Two in a row felt like it meant something about how the rotation was running that day, so I built in a forward shift
I signed and released with the figures as they stood. I weighed the delay risk against a one-bag discrepancy
